overview: The paper proposes Generative Diffusion Prior Distillation (GDPD), a knowledge distillation framework that models teacher knowledge as a generative diffusion prior over full-context features to guide the training of partial time-series classifiers, using posterior sampling to provide dynamic, diverse, and collective supervision signals.

modules.name: Data Preprocessing Module
modules.description: Responsible for transforming raw time series data (UCR, UEA, PhysioNet) into standardized, normalized sequences of uniform length, and generating corresponding truncated prefixes and channel-wise masks to simulate partial observability.

modules.name: Data Loader Module
modules.description: Responsible for converting preprocessed data into batched tensors, yielding dictionaries containing full-length inputs, partial inputs (time-wise truncated and/or channel-wise masked), and corresponding labels for both teacher and student training.

modules.name: Backbone Architectures Module
modules.description: Responsible for implementing the time-series classification networks (LSTM, InceptionTime, ResNet) with specific architectural splits to expose intermediate feature representations (feature extractor and classification head) for knowledge distillation.

modules.name: Diffusion Prior Network Module
modules.description: Responsible for implementing the lightweight denoiser network operating in the feature space and the noise fusing block that initializes the reverse diffusion process by adaptively fusing student features with Gaussian noise.

modules.name: Diffusion Process Module
modules.description: Responsible for defining the forward diffusion trajectory to corrupt teacher features into noise and the reverse DDIM sampling trajectory to iteratively restore plausible full-context features conditioned on the noisy initialization.

modules.name: Standard KD Baselines Module
modules.description: Responsible for implementing various knowledge distillation loss functions (Logit-KD, Feature-KD, RKD, VID, DKD, Attention, etc.) to provide comparative baselines aligning student and teacher outputs.

modules.name: GDPD Loss Module
modules.description: Responsible for computing the generative distillation loss by performing posterior sampling using the diffusion prior conditioned on student features, and then evaluating the classification loss of the student head on the reconstructed target features.

modules.name: Training Orchestrator Module
modules.description: Responsible for managing the two-phase training schedule (warm-up phase for diffusion prior and guided phase for GDPD), coordinating the forward/backward passes, and updating model parameters based on the combined task and distillation losses.

modules.name: Evaluation Metrics Module
modules.description: Responsible for calculating classification performance metrics (AUC-PRC, AUC-ROC, Accuracy) and distillation fidelity metrics (Teacher-Student Top-1 Agreement) from model predictions and ground truth labels.

modules.name: Suffix Transferability Module
modules.description: Responsible for evaluating the representation learning capability of prefix-trained students by assessing their performance on suffix inputs through linear probing and zero-shot classification protocols.

modules.name: Ablation Study Runner Module
modules.description: Responsible for executing controlled experiments by systematically varying critical hyperparameters (warm-up epochs, distillation weights, diffusion steps, posterior samples) to analyze their impact on model performance.

modules.name: Experiment Configuration Module
modules.description: Responsible for parsing and managing experimental setups, including dataset specifications, earliness levels, model architectures, and optimization hyperparameters, to ensure reproducible and structured experiment execution.

modules.name: Results Aggregation Module
modules.description: Responsible for synthesizing raw metric outputs across multiple datasets and runs into statistical summaries (Average Rank, Top-1 Wins, Wins/Draws/Losses) and generating formatted LaTeX tables and comparison charts.
